question_text: A spring stores 60 J before launch. After launch it is relaxed and the car has 36 J of kinetic energy. The remaining energy is thermal within the system. No energy crosses the boundary.

parts.text: Calculate the thermal energy increase and useful-output efficiency.
Describe final energy bars and explain conservation.
Predict what happens to useful output if friction is reduced with the same initial energy, and justify.

correct_answer.model_response:
a) Thermal increase = 60 − 36 = 24 J. Efficiency = 36/60 × 100 = 60%.
b) Elastic 0 J; kinetic 36 J; thermal increase 24 J. Total 60 J equals the initial total.
c) Less energy is transferred into thermal energy by friction, so more can remain as useful kinetic energy, assuming other changes are negligible. Total energy still cannot exceed the input.

explanation:
a) Thermal increase = 60 − 36 = 24 J. Efficiency = 36/60 × 100 = 60%.
b) Elastic 0 J; kinetic 36 J; thermal increase 24 J. Total 60 J equals the initial total.
c) Less energy is transferred into thermal energy by friction, so more can remain as useful kinetic energy, assuming other changes are negligible. Total energy still cannot exceed the input.

marking_rubric.criterion: 24 J thermal increase
60% efficiency
Correct final bar values
Conserved total 60 J
Predicts greater useful kinetic energy
Explains reduced thermal transfer under stated conditions
